title: Infrared Divergences as Itinerant Vacua
abstract: Infrared divergences (IRDs) are usually treated as pathologies to be cancelled, regularized, or hidden in dressed asymptotic states. This paper develops a complementary and constructive viewpoint: an IRD is the signature of an \emph{itinerant vacuum} -- a quantum vacuum that wanders continuously through a family of inequivalent states as a classical order parameter evolves. Each value of the order parameter carries its own coherent vacuum, so moving the order parameter means traversing a succession of orthogonal vacua. The IRD is the field-theoretic cost of this wandering, and the $1/f$ noise, gravitational memory, and non-Gaussian fluctuations that emerge from it are its observable classical remnants.   The technical core is an exact separation in the real-time closed-time-path (CTP) effective action. The infrared-divergent imaginary part of the influence functional must not be left as a divergent coefficient in a deterministic equation of motion; it is instead converted, by a Hubbard--Stratonovich identity, into a classical stochastic source. This step is an algebraic identity of the generating functional and requires no prior coarse graining or decoherence assumption: the retarded kernel encodes the memory of past vacuum transitions, while the noise kernel encodes the quantum uncertainty of the next one. We apply this construction to four parallel arenas -- soft QED, scalar fields in de Sitter space, soft gravitons, and non-equilibrium phase transitions -- and show that the same itinerant-vacuum mechanism underlies $1/f$ current noise, the primordial power spectrum, gravitational memory, and order-parameter dynamics. A geometric formulation in terms of a Hilbert-space bundle over the vacuum manifold is outlined as an outlook.
summary: This paper reinterprets infrared divergences not as calculation errors but as physical signatures of an 'itinerant vacuum' undergoing continuous transitions. By employing the closed-time-path effective action, it rigorously derives how these divergences generate observable classical stochastic noise sources. This unified framework successfully explains $1/f$ noise and memory effects across soft QED, cosmology, and general non-equilibrium physics.
main_problem: The paper develops a constructive viewpoint for Infrared Divergences (IRDs), treating them not as pathologies to be removed, but as signatures of an "itinerant vacuum." This framework aims to unify the origin of various noise sources in non-equilibrium quantum systems.
main_result: IRDs are shown to manifest as a classical stochastic source term within the real-time effective action, unifying phenomena like $1/f$ current noise, primordial power spectra, and gravitational memory under one mechanism.
method: The core method involves an exact separation in the closed-time-path (CTP) effective action, converting the imaginary part of the influence functional into a classical stochastic source via a Hubbard–Stratonovich identity.
model_or_system: The theory is applied to several physical arenas: soft QED, scalar fields evolving in de Sitter space, soft gravitons, and general non-equilibrium phase transitions where a classical order parameter evolves through inequivalent quantum vacua.
key_observables: $1/f$ noise spectrum (e.g., $S_J(\omega) \propto 1/|\omega|$), gravitational memory effects, and non-Gaussian fluctuations in order parameters.
important_parameters: The infrared cutoff ($\omega_{	ext{IR}}$) is central; the analysis relies on the structure of the retarded kernel (memory) versus the noise kernel (uncertainty).
main_assumptions: The approach requires no prior coarse graining or decoherence assumption, deriving stochasticity directly from the CTP effective action's imaginary part.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first establishing the general formalism using the CTP effective action to generate Langevin equations. It then applies this framework systematically to soft QED (soft photons), soft gravitons, and non-equilibrium transitions, demonstrating consistency across these disparate physical systems.
why_interesting: It provides a powerful, unified mathematical tool—the stochastic source derived from IR divergences in the CTP formalism—to model complex, open quantum system dynamics without resorting to standard environment splitting assumptions common in AMO physics.
